issues.reason: The half that stands: `high` is outside the stated marker set for the `quantity` scale (excessive / insufficient / sufficient) and the documented amount-Degree sits on the noun's witness, so the atom is off-spec; the half that falls: it is a defect — the atom is true of the sentence, coins no head, and 'high levels of <bare mass>' is exactly the coverage gap the reviewer's own q2 logs, while dropping the unrepresentable `level` head is the instruction set's stated preference over mis-slotting it.

The half that stands: sealing a complement that is itself a generic is unaddressed; the half that falls: the cited bars — `(Implication …)` is an atom and *Core patterns* seals several atoms as `(And …)`, each `$x` is bound by its own implication exactly as in the two top-level rules the same parse emits, and the universal distributes over the conjunction so the shared variable name asserts nothing about a leaf being both green and black.

The bare-plural-is-generic test is stated as the determiner choice for copular categoricals, and the verbal generic rule it would force here ('every study found this') would be flatly false, whereas `(GroupOf sk_studies_1 study)` is true and well-typed improvisation in the episodic-bare-plural gap the reviewer's own q2 concedes.

gaps_confirmed: existential / episodic bare-plural subject ('Studies have found that P') — bare plurals are routed only to the generic kind/rule reading

'high levels of <mass>' — a qualitative, non-numeric amount of a bare mass has no licensed carrier (Measure needs magnitude+unit, ProportionOf needs a whole, Degree's quantity slot has three fixed markers)
an attitude complement that is itself a generic — sealing an `(Implication …)` under Theme is unaddressed
'find (that)' appears in neither the factive nor the non-factive list, so P's projection is left to the parser
new_gaps: the instruction set fixes no bearer type for `Degree` (entity vs eventuality), unlike the Member/Inheritance and LocatedIn/Location disciplines, so an amount modifier whose noun has no witness has no stated anchor
notes: `Experiencer` on the find event is licensed by *Propositional attitudes*, which prescribes Experiencer for that-clause attitudes including the factives, notwithstanding the progressive test in *Thematic roles*.
